title: Officer shooting of suspect on Hwy. 417 not a criminal offence, SIU finds
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has ruled that an Ottawa police officer who shot and killed a man near Highway 417 and Walkley Road didn't commit a criminal offence.
Richard Bastien, 43, of Montreal, was shot when he got out of his car in Ottawa's south end at around 5:30 p.m. April 22, following a police chase.
After Bastien's vehicle stopped, he got out carrying a revolver, said police.
An officer fired a number of shots and Bastien was struck.
He was taken to the Civic campus of the Ottawa Hospital, where he died of his injuries two days later.
The SIU, a civilian agency that investigates cases of serious injury involving police, was called in to investigate the shooting.
The agency concluded that there were no reasonable grounds to believe that the shooting had been a criminal offence, said SIU director Ian Scott Friday.

"It appears that Mr. Bastien pointed his revolver at a witness officer and also in the direction of the subject officer," said Scott, who noted that the subject officer - the one who shot the suspect - had fired from inside his cruiser.
"Almost simultaneously, Mr. Bastien shot himself in the left temple area of his head," said Scott.
"According to the autopsy, the self-inflicted wound, and not the wound inflicted by the officer, was the fatal one."

An officer who fires his weapon is permitted to use such force - according to the Criminal Code - when he believes, on reasonable grounds, that it is necessary for his self preservation or for the preservation of anyone under his protection, Scott said.
